To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a steady-state centrally fuelled plasma generates a current that is proportional to the thermonuclear heating power.
(a) a transport driven current is predicted by the kinetic models, (b) the current is of order one mega-amp for ITER type discharges and (c) it is not affected by collisionality.
the collisional kinetic theory of transport driven currents in centrally fuelled discharges predicts a current of the order of one mega-amp for ITER type discharges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a kinetic theory of the transport driven current and its application to the analysis of centrally fuelled tokamak discharges.

the development of first-principle kinetic theory for collisional and collisionless plasma transport, and with the identification and analysis of new phenomena, such as transport driven current, which may be relevant in the design of fusion reactors.
the development of analytical and numerical models for the study of the physics of the plasma edge in magnetically confined fusion plasmas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the collisionless transport driven current in central fuelling plasmas is a real physical effect, and that the collisional relaxation of the velocity distribution function is the mechanism that drives this current.
the transport driven current exists, and is a significant effect in the central region of a steady-state tokamak with central fuelling.
the transport driven current is a robust phenomenon in centrally fuelled steady state discharges.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a collisionless transport driven current exists in centrally fuelled steady state tokamak discharges, and that this current can be as large as one mega-amp in ITER type discharges.
the analytical model predicts that the collisionless radial flux is canonically related to a transport driven current.

the collisionless transport driven current in steady-state plasmas is a robust and generic phenomenon, and its collisional extension is analytically described by the first-principles collisional kinetic model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transport driven current is a canonical invariant of the radial electron flux.
the transport driven current can be used as a new tool for plasma control in tokamaks.
the transport driven current is a robust feature of collisionless and collisional plasmas and it is expected to be present in any tokamak operating in the central fuelled mode.
